newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar builds on gains, eyes resistance.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar builds on gains, eyes resistance.

text.p: London's August white sugar contract built on its recent gains on Tuesday amid fears of seasonal tightness and gathered momentum to mount a challenge of nearby resistance at $317.50, traders said.

August burst higher during Monday's session to hit an intraday high of $317.00 on a mixture of broker, trade and commission buying, with the bullish sentiment heightened by strength in New York's July contract.
Traders said the interest on Tuesday appeared to be more concentrated in the August/October spread, which has widened from $8.00 to $11.00 in a matter of days.
August/October was crossed at $11.30 while the highest outright trade was at $11.00. One leading commission was reported to be a good buyer.
At 1100 GMT all positions were slightly firmer. August was up 40 cents at $317.00 after hitting an intraday high of $317.40. October was up 20 cents at $306.40 and volume totalled a light 333 lots.
Traders said the market might not be able to maintain its current strength for long without more profit-taking, even though there was more room to the upside.
"It is a fact as it stands but I just don't think it's going to be sustained," said one.
But London could see another surge if July raws hits 11.10 cents/lb where buy stops are thought to be placed.
Traders said traditional concerns about being short of the August position at the tail-end of European availability and ahead of the new crop were supporting the market, if not driving it higher.
Russian demand for European white sugar, despite hefty duties, would also keep London futures supported as would offtake from Iran, Pakistan and Bangladesh.
Iran tendered again on Monday to buy white sugar but is not thought to have bought as prices are high.

Pakistan has been a regular importer of lesser-quality sugars in recent weeks and Bangladesh is believed to have an import requirement of around 50,000 tonnes of crystals, to be hedged against the London market.
The Paris market was dull with just 11 lots traded of the August contract, up 40 cents at $317.20.
